title: Career roadmap · Reservoir Engineer
summary: Build toward reservoir-engineering roles involving subsurface evaluation, reservoir characterisation, fluid-flow modelling, reserves estimation, production forecasting, simulation and field-development planning.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 4-year B.Tech/B.E. program from 2026–2030. Reservoir-engineering roles can become highly specialised and may require strong mathematics, simulation skills, petroleum-geoscience knowledge and industry experience.

about.label: Mapping
about.text: Reservoir Engineer is directly aligned with Petroleum Engineering.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build petroleum fundamentals, geology, fluid properties, reservoir rock/fluid behaviour, well testing, material balance, numerical methods and simulation skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop expertise in reservoir simulation, enhanced oil recovery, field development, reserves, production forecasting or subsurface data analytics.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Senior Reservoir Engineer, Reservoir Simulation Engineer, Field Development Engineer or Subsurface Team Lead.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine reservoir engineering with AI, digital twins, uncertainty analysis, carbon storage, geothermal systems and low-carbon energy applications.

rows.text: Geology, fluid mechanics and petroleum fundamentals
Reservoir rock/fluid properties, petrophysics and fluid flow
Material balance, PVT, well testing and reservoir performance
Reservoir simulation, numerical methods and production forecasting
History matching, uncertainty, EOR and field-development planning
Reservoir economics, reserves, integrated subsurface workflows and data analytics

blocks.text: Use additional credits for advanced reservoir simulation, geostatistics, numerical methods, enhanced oil recovery, uncertainty quantification, machine learning for subsurface engineering, carbon storage or energy-system research.

Reservoir engineering is expanding beyond conventional oil and gas into digital subsurface modelling, carbon storage, geothermal energy and advanced recovery. Strong fundamentals in fluid flow and reservoir simulation remain valuable while data science and uncertainty analysis become increasingly important.

items: Graduate Engineer Trainee / Junior Reservoir Engineer (0–2 years)
Senior Reservoir Engineer / Simulation Engineer (5–8 years)
Reservoir Engineering Lead / Field Development Engineer (8–12 years)
Reservoir Engineering Manager / Subsurface Technical Specialist (12+ years)

blocks.text: A PhD is most relevant for advanced subsurface research, R&D, academia and specialised energy technology.

Reservoir engineering is likely to expand beyond conventional hydrocarbon development into carbon storage, geothermal energy, underground energy storage and advanced subsurface modelling. Build strong expertise in fluid flow, numerical simulation and uncertainty while learning data science and AI methods that can improve reservoir forecasting and decision-making.
